key_insight: A quasi-square-wave spanwise wall oscillation reveals that drag reduction comes from phase-dependent switching of the self-sustaining process: it is suppressed during sustained Stokes strain and recovers when the strain passes through zero.
engineering_relevance: Duty-cycle shaping of wall oscillation can outperform a sinusoidal baseline, improving gross drag reduction by 2.5 percentage points while making the causal mechanism more controllable and observable.
method: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent channel flow at friction Reynolds number ~200 with spanwise wall actuation.
Use of a quasi-square-wave waveform to separate each cycle into Reversal and Displacement phases.
Phase-resolved and stochastic enstrophy-budget analysis to track SSP dynamics and vorticity redistribution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports phase-resolved observations and a stochastic enstrophy-budget analysis, and notes a 2.5 percentage-point improvement in gross drag-reduction margin over the optimal sinusoidal case.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated at moderate Reynolds number in DNS, so practical performance may depend on actuation hardware limits and how well the phase timing transfers to higher-Re flows.
paper_title: Duty-cycle modulation of the self-sustaining process by spanwise wall oscillation
